scenes.title: Forward, backward, update: who writes which buffer
scenes.description: Press Forward, Backward and Update one at a time. Watch which buffer each step writes: backward fills the gradient buffers, and only the update changes w and b.

args: It read w and b and saved

cues.text: Each button runs exactly one step of the training loop.
Backward writes gradients; only Update writes parameters.

accessibility.text: One training example with x = 2, target y = 3, starting parameters w = 0.5 and b = 0, learning rate 0.1. Program: p = w*x + b, L = (p - y)^2/2, then L.backward(), then the update w -= lr*w.grad and b -= lr*b.grad, then the gradients are cleared. Forward computes p = 1 and loss 2 and changes no parameter. Backward writes the gradient buffers w.grad = -4 and b.grad = -2; w is still 0.5 and b is still 0. Update subtracts learning rate times gradient: w = 0.5 - 0.1*(-4) = 0.9 and b = 0 - 0.1*(-2) = 0.2, then clears the gradients. A fresh forward gives p = 2 and loss 0.5. A second backward at the new parameters gives w.grad = -2 and b.grad = -1. The Forward, Backward, Update and Reset buttons, or the phase selector, move one step at a time; the highlighted code line, the memory readouts and the graph show the same step.
